Topic: FilteredElementCollector
Class: FilteredElementCollector (Namespace: Autodesk.Revit.DB)
Summary: Core search engine for querying elements within a Revit document.
Code Pattern:
collector = FilteredElementCollector(doc).OfCategory(BuiltInCategory.OST_Walls).WhereElementIsNotElementType().ToElements()
Best Practices: Always chain Quick Filters (OfCategory, OfClass) before Slow Filters. Use WhereElementIsNotElementType() to exclude family symbols. For view-specific queries, pass view.Id: FilteredElementCollector(doc, view.Id).
Common Pitfalls: Avoid iterating over whole document when a view collector is sufficient. ToElements() instantiates Python lists; for large sets prefer lazy iteration directly over the collector.

Topic: Transactions and Document Modification
Class: Transaction (Namespace: Autodesk.Revit.DB)
Summary: Context for modifying document state. Required for creating, deleting, or altering elements.
Code Pattern:
from pyrevit import revit
with revit.Transaction('Action Name'):
    element.LookupParameter('Comments').Set('Updated')
Best Practices: In pyRevit, wrap operations inside with revit.Transaction('Name'): block. Keep transactions as short and scoped as possible.
Common Pitfalls: Starting a transaction during read-only events causes InvalidOperationException. Forgetting to commit or roll back unhandled exceptions can lock Revit.

Topic: Drafting and View Management
Class: ViewDrafting (Namespace: Autodesk.Revit.DB)
Summary: Specialized 2D views that do not display 3D model geometry.
Code Pattern:
views = FilteredElementCollector(doc).OfClass(ViewDrafting).ToElements()
Best Practices: Filter out ViewDrafting elements where view.IsTemplate is True before evaluating element counts. Use FilteredElementCollector(doc, view.Id).GetElementCount() for fast zero-element checks.
Common Pitfalls: Attempting to query 3D elements inside drafting views yields empty sets. Deleting an active view causes UI crashes.

Topic: Workset Querying and Assignment
Class: FilteredWorksetCollector (Namespace: Autodesk.Revit.DB)
Summary: Collects user-created and standard worksets in workshared models.
Code Pattern:
worksets = FilteredWorksetCollector(doc).OfKind(WorksetKind.UserWorkset).ToWorksets()
Best Practices: Always verify doc.IsWorkshared before instantiating FilteredWorksetCollector. Handle non-workshared models gracefully.
Common Pitfalls: Modifying worksets requires active central file connectivity. Attempting workset actions on standard non-workshared .rvt files raises InvalidOperationException.

Topic: Parameter Access and Modification
Class: Parameter (Namespace: Autodesk.Revit.DB)
Summary: Element data holder. Access via BuiltInParameter or name lookup.
Code Pattern:
param = element.get_Parameter(BuiltInParameter.ALL_MODEL_MARK)
if param and not param.IsReadOnly:
    param.Set('NEW_MARK')
Best Practices: Prefer get_Parameter(BuiltInParameter) over LookupParameter(str) for performance and language independence. Check param.IsReadOnly before Set().
Common Pitfalls: LookupParameter returns None if parameter does not exist; calling .Set() directly causes AttributeError.
